Consequently, Tata Sons must remain subject to NBFC-Upper Layer regulations for at least five years, prompting a planned public listing valued at Rs 2.01 lakh crore.
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India rejected Tata Sons' request to surrender its Certificate of Registration in a letter dated September 11, 2026. The central bank advised the entity to ensure full compliance with NBFC-Upper Layer guidelines, noting its assets of Rs 2.01 lakh crore exceed the Rs 1 lakh crore threshold. This decision means Tata Sons will remain under stricter regulatory frameworks for at least five years, leading to a looming listing.
items.title: RBI denies Tata Sons deregistration request, forcing upcoming listing

key_points: BRICS leaders unanimously approved the 45-page New Delhi Declaration, which backs a two-state solution for Palestine and opposes unilateral tariffs.
The declaration condemned the April 2025 Pahalgam terror attack and called for Israel to withdraw forces from Lebanon.
Member states expressed support for India and Brazil's UN Security Council aspirations and committed to implementing the BRICS AI governance statement.
items.summary: BRICS nations unanimously approved the 45-page New Delhi Declaration during the summit led by India on Saturday. The document expresses serious concerns regarding the rise of unilateral tariffs and non-tariff measures that distort trade. It reiterates support for a two-state solution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict and calls for stronger international institutional backing for Palestine. The declaration also condemned the April 2025 terror attack in Pahalgam, which killed 26 people, and urged Israel to withdraw from Lebanese territory. Additionally, BRICS members voiced support for India and Brazil's aspirations to join the UN Security Council and committed to implementing the grouping's statement on global AI governance.
items.title: BRICS nations approve New Delhi Declaration supporting two-state solution

key_points: Weibo leaker Instant Digital reports that Samsung Display has secured a three-year exclusive supply agreement for Apple's foldable iPhone Duo.
The South Korean company is reportedly charging Apple approximately $250 for each inner folding display panel, a figure significantly higher than standard OLED costs.
Apple has not publicly confirmed the agreement or the specific pricing details associated with the reported supply contract.
items.summary: According to Weibo leaker Instant Digital, Samsung Display has signed a three-year exclusive supply agreement with Apple for the foldable iPhone Duo and future models. The South Korean company is reportedly charging Apple around $250 for each inner folding display panel, a cost that would represent roughly one-eighth of the device's estimated $1,999 starting price. Apple has not publicly confirmed either the reported agreement or the specific price tag. If accurate, the deal would give Samsung a major role in Apple's entry into the foldable smartphone market, relying on Samsung's M16 OLED material set and high-strength glass layers to ensure durability. Industry reports suggest Apple may have concerns regarding BOE's foldable panels, further strengthening Samsung's position as a primary supplier for this technically demanding component.
items.title: Samsung Display signs exclusive three-year deal for Apple foldable iPhone

key_points: All survivors were treated at a local hospital before being safely repatriated to Bangladesh following the high waves and strong currents that caused the accident.
items.summary: The Border Security Force rescued 10 Bangladeshi nationals, including an infant, after their boat capsized in the Padma River in Murshidabad, West Bengal. High waves and strong currents caused the vessel to overturn, sweeping passengers away before BSF personnel spotted them and launched a rescue operation using a speed boat. All survivors received medical evaluation and treatment at a local hospital before being safely repatriated to Bangladesh.
items.title: BSF rescues 10 Bangladeshis including infant after boat capsizes in Padma River

key_points: Yemen's Saudi-backed government forces reported striking Houthi fighters in Mocha, while the Houthis claimed Saudi aircraft conducted 129 airstrikes over 48 hours.
The renewed conflict has displaced 76,000 people since July, with the UN warning that needs are outpacing available support.
items.summary: Yemen's Saudi-backed government forces stated on September 12, 2026, that they struck Iran-allied Houthi fighters in the Red Sea city of Mocha. The Houthis reported Saudi aircraft conducted 129 airstrikes on their controlled areas during the same period. Since July, the UN migration agency reported that 76,000 people have fled the fighting, a number that quadrupled in one week. The agency warned that humanitarian needs are far outpacing what they can deliver.
items.title: Yemeni forces strike Houthi targets in Red Sea city of Mocha

key_points: Harish Rao demanded the resignation of Revenue Minister Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy and clarification on the Section 22-A prohibited lands list.
items.summary: Former minister and BRS deputy floor leader T. Harish Rao rejected allegations of wrongdoing in a land deal involving his father-in-law. He stated the land was allotted by the Congress government in 1995, with payment and mutation also occurring under that administration. Rao accused the current government of diverting attention from the Section 22-A issue by making personal allegations and demanded the resignation of Revenue Minister Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy.
items.title: Harish Rao Rejects Land Deal Allegations Against His Father-in-Law

key_points: Students and activists in Hyderabad protested on Saturday demanding the release of Noida workers detained following April labour protests.
Organisers cited an Allahabad High Court order regarding Aakriti Chaudhary while activists alleged illegal arrests and custodial torture in multiple cases.
items.summary: Students, activists and citizens protested in Hyderabad on Saturday demanding the release of Noida workers arrested after April labour protests. Organised by CaRWAN, the demonstration alleged that many detainees remain in jail for five months through multiple cases. Activists cited an Allahabad High Court order quashing the NSA detention of Aakriti Chaudhary, though they noted she remains in custody in other matters. Disha Students' Organisation activist Mahipal alleged that 11 FIRs were filed over the same episode, accusing police of illegal arrests and custodial torture. Protesters demanded unconditional release of the workers and an end to what they described as police repression.
items.title: Activists Protest in Hyderabad Over Noida Worker Arrests

key_points: A 73-year-old labourer in Indore lost Rs 3.34 lakh after an unidentified person used his lost mobile phone to transfer money via UPI.
items.summary: Madanlal Chauhan, a 73-year-old labourer in Indore, reported losing Rs 3.34 lakh after an unidentified person used his lost phone to make unauthorized UPI transactions. The suspect transferred the money between March 16 and March 21, 2025, after activating a PhonePe account on the device. Following the discovery, Chauhan filed a cybercrime complaint, prompting Sanwer police to register a case under sections 318(4) of the BNS and 66D of the IT Act while investigating the fraudulent activity.
items.title: Lost Phone Leads to Rs 3.34 Lakh Fraud Against Indore Labourer

key_points: Ananth Narayan Gopalakrishnan explains that SEBI adopted a calibrated approach to reduce F&O risks through consultation rather than immediate bans.
The former regulator states that the RBI's FCNR(B) swap scheme creates economic costs for the system while benefiting foreign banks and Indian lenders.
Gopalakrishnan argues that allowing markets to signal natural prices is essential to fix distortions in India's tax regime and interest rates.
He notes that no currency currently replaces the US dollar, though central banks are diversifying reserves amid geopolitical tensions.
items.summary: Ananth Narayan Gopalakrishnan, a former Whole-Time Member of SEBI, discusses financial market challenges in an interview with BusinessLine. He explains that SEBI reduced weekly index-option expiries after consultations rather than banning them, citing concerns over retail losses and market stability. Regarding the RBI's FCNR(B) swap facility, Gopalakrishnan estimates the scheme costs the system roughly $14-15 billion in present value, noting that domestic savers likely bear opportunity costs through lower deposit rates. He advocates for less market distortion in interest rates and a neutral tax regime to improve competitiveness. Finally, he observes that while central banks are diversifying reserves, no currency currently rivals the US dollar's dominance in global transactions.
items.title: Former SEBI official discusses F&O risks and RBI swap costs

key_points: The Food Safety Administration conducted surprise inspections at five major hotels in Indore and found various hygiene and safety irregularities.
items.summary: The Food Safety Administration conducted surprise inspections at five major hotels in Indore on Saturday, uncovering significant hygiene and safety irregularities. Senior food safety officer Manish Swami informed Free Press that officials checked storage, labelling, and kitchen conditions at Hotel Marriott, Hotel The Park, Radisson Blu, Radisson RED, and Hotel Grand Sheraton. Violations included waterlogging, rusting equipment, improper labelling, and missing medical fitness records. The administration stated that notices are being issued to establishments where violations were found and that no negligence related to food quality or consumer health will be tolerated.
items.title: Food Inspections Reveal Hygiene Lapses At Five Top City Hotels

key_points: Former Ambassador Ashok Kantha told India Today that India must approach China in a hard-headed manner while maintaining border peace.
NITI Aayog CEO Amitabh Kant stated that China weaponizes technology and urged BRICS members to demand manufacturing access.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian dismissed accusations of foreign military aid and confirmed the supreme leader remains in power.
items.summary: Strategic experts debated the state of India-China relations following high-level engagements, with former Ambassador Ashok Kantha emphasizing a hard-headed approach to bilateral disputes. Kantha told India Today that normalization depends on border tranquility and noted structural issues like trade deficits and Chinese support to Pakistan. Meanwhile, Amitabh Kant highlighted how China dominates clean energy processing and called for BRICS reforms to counter US trade policies. In separate news, severe flooding submerged villages in West Bengal's Malda district, forcing medical staff to operate amid darkness. Additionally, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian addressed regional security, stating Russia and China are friends while condemning US and Israel actions as state terror.
items.title: Experts debate India-China relations amid trade deficits and border tensions

key_points: The New York Post reported that Donald Trump's childhood home in Queens sold for $1.93 million after a major renovation.
Developer Tommy Lin purchased the neglected property for $835,000 and spent an additional $500,000 to modernize the five-bedroom residence.
The house previously sold for $2.14 million in 2017 and was later listed for $2.9 million before falling into disrepair.
items.summary: The New York Post reported that President Donald Trump's childhood home in Queens, New York, sold for $1.93 million following a significant renovation. Developer Tommy Lin acquired the neglected Tudor-style property last year for $835,000 and invested another $500,000 over eight months to transform the water-damaged house into a modern residence. The home, built by Fred Trump in 1940, had reportedly been occupied by feral cats before the overhaul. Previous sales data indicates the property changed hands for $2.14 million in 2017 and was listed for $2.9 million in 2019 before deteriorating further.
items.title: Trump childhood Queens home sold after renovation for $1.93 million

key_points: Trump later acknowledged there is no good answer to the reunification question while addressing business leaders.
items.summary: US President Donald Trump told reporters in Dublin that a unified Ireland would be fantastic and might happen eventually. He added that the UK would have something to say about it. Later, addressing business leaders, Trump acknowledged there is no good answer to the reunification question. The statement may draw mixed reactions from the Irish people, as the issue remains deeply sensitive due to historical divisions between nationalists and unionists.
items.title: Trump says unified Ireland would be fantastic during Dublin visit

key_points: An ASLI-JLL report states India's senior living market is expected to become a $10.1 billion opportunity by 2030, requiring $7.7 billion in capital investment.
The report highlights a shortage of assisted living beds, with current supply at 2,100 against a projected need of 11,000 by 2030.
items.summary: An ASLI-JLL report titled 'India's Silver Economy: From Niche to Necessity' projects that India's senior living market will reach $10. 1 billion by 2030. G. Rajagopal of ASLI noted that while the market is growing, it currently has only 1. 5% penetration compared to higher rates in the U. S. and New Zealand. Karan Singh Sodi of JLL emphasized a critical shortage of assisted living beds, which stand at 2,100 today against a projected need of 11,000 by 2030. The report identifies skilled caregiver shortages and high real estate costs as key constraints.
items.title: ASLI-JLL report forecasts India's senior living market to reach $10.1 billion by 2030

key_points: TMC supremo Mamata Banerjee contacted veteran Akhil Giri and requested a meeting regarding the upcoming Nandigram bypoll, though the party has not officially announced a candidate.
Akhil Giri stated he shared his views on the matter via WhatsApp and emphasized that the final decision rests with Banerjee, while suggesting a local candidate would be preferable.

The bypoll occurs amidst an internal crisis where a rebel faction claims the party symbol and threatens to contest as independents if the Election Commission does not rule in their favor before nominations close.
items.summary: TMC leader Mamata Banerjee reached out to veteran Akhil Giri, asking him to meet at her Kalighat residence to discuss the upcoming Nandigram bypoll. A TMC leader from Banerjee's camp reported that Banerjee sought Giri's opinion, and Giri conveyed his suggestions via WhatsApp while stating the final decision rests with the party supremo. Giri argued for a local candidate but pledged to abide by the leadership's choice. This move comes as the TMC faces an organizational crisis following its May election loss to the BJP. A rival faction led by Ritabrata Banerjee claims the party's name and symbol, creating uncertainty about who will field a candidate. Senior leader Abu Taher also questioned why Banerjee should not contest personally instead of nominating a local figure. The bypoll serves as a critical test for the TMC to rebuild its influence in a constituency that once defined its rise.
items.title: Mamata Banerjee contacts Akhil Giri as TMC considers Nandigram bypoll candidate

key_points: Analysts recommend existing investors hold Asian Paints shares but advise against new entries due to a demanding valuation of 50 times trailing earnings.
The company faces intensified competition from Birla Opus and JSW Dulux, which has forced higher marketing spends and reduced pricing power in FY26.
While Q1FY27 showed strong revenue growth and margin expansion, analysts warn that higher-cost raw material inventory could weigh on future performance.
items.summary: Analysts report that Asian Paints remains India's leading decorative paints player but faces a competitive reset from new capacity, particularly from Birla Opus. The article states the stock trades at about 50 times trailing earnings, a level first seen in December 2020, making the risk-reward unappealing for fresh entry. While Q1FY27 revenue rose 17.9% year on year to ₹10,542 crore, the company's FY26 value growth was only 5.3% despite volume growth of 9%. Management indicated demand remained healthy with no meaningful inventory build-up, yet higher-cost raw material inventory is expected to impact Q2. The analysts conclude that while the company's scale and backward-integration investments provide strength, the balance of volume growth and margin protection currently supports a hold rather than a buy.
items.title: Analysts advise Asian Paints investors to hold stock amid competitive pressure

key_points: A 2025 report estimates ice on Mt Kenya, Kilimanjaro, and Rwenzori has shrunk 96% over 115 years and will disappear in three to five years.
Senior Scientist Rainer Prinz explains that reduced snowfall driven by Indian Ocean temperature patterns, rather than direct warming, is the primary cause of this unprecedented retreat.
The loss will eliminate unique high-altitude habitats and scientific research sites, though it will not significantly impact regional water flows as forests serve as the true water towers.
items.summary: East Africa's iconic mountain glaciers on Mt Kenya, Kilimanjaro, and Rwenzori are projected to vanish within three to five years, according to a 2025 State of the Climate in Africa report. The report notes a 96% reduction in ice area on Mt Kenya over the past 115 years. Senior Scientist Rainer Prinz attributes this unprecedented retreat primarily to declining snowfall caused by shifting sea surface temperatures in the Indian Ocean, rather than direct temperature increases. While the disappearance will eliminate unique high-altitude habitats and valuable scientific research sites, the article clarifies that these glaciers do not significantly function as water reservoirs for the region. Instead, forests provide the essential water supply, meaning glacier loss will not directly alter current freshwater flows despite the ecological and spiritual consequences of losing these white mountain tops.
items.title: East Africa's mountain glaciers will vanish within five years

key_points: The regulator suggested using a blended volume-weighted average price for settlement or temporarily reverting to the pre-CAS mechanism while discontinuing the display of indicative index values.
items.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India proposed reviewing expiry-day settlement prices, market timings, and information dissemination under the Closing Auction Session following industry feedback on initial operational snags. In a consultation paper released on September 12, the regulator suggested using a blended volume-weighted average price or temporarily reverting to the pre-CAS mechanism for settlement. Additionally, SEBI proposed discontinuing the display of indicative index values to prevent market misinterpretation.
items.title: SEBI proposes tweaks to Closing Auction Session after industry feedback

key_points: Cockroach Janta Party co-founder Ashutosh Ranka identified teacher shortages, poor hygiene, and recruitment irregularities during school audits in Bengaluru.
Ranka stated that no paper leaks in Karnataka will be tolerated and confirmed the party will launch a structured campaign against the KPSC scam.
items.summary: Cockroach Janta Party co-founder Ashutosh Ranka highlighted teacher deployment issues, poor school hygiene, and recruitment irregularities after auditing government schools in Bengaluru. Ranka asserted that no paper leaks in Karnataka will be tolerated, promising a structured campaign against the KPSC scam while maintaining solidarity with affected students.
items.title: CJP's Ranka vows zero tolerance for KPSC paper leaks in Karnataka

key_points: BRICS leaders on Saturday condemned the April 2025 Pahalgam terror attack and called for combating terrorism in all its forms, including cross-border movement and financing.
items.summary: BRICS leaders on Saturday condemned the April 2025 Pahalgam terror attack and called for combating terrorism in all its forms, including cross-border movement and financing. The attack killed 26 people, mostly Hindus, prompting India to launch military strikes in Pakistan that were met with retaliatory shelling before an understanding was reached on May 10. This marks the second consecutive year the grouping has condemned the incident in its declaration.
items.title: BRICS leaders condemn Pahalgam terror attack and call for global action against terrorism

key_points: AAP hoardings signaling a potential alliance with Vijai Sardesai's GFP surfaced in Goa, while AAP convenor Arvind Kejriwal announced an imminent declaration.
Goa Congress president Girish Chodankar stated that alliance talks with the GFP remain ongoing, noting the party had stalled previous discussions due to a lack of response.
items.summary: Hoardings featuring the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and Goa Forward Party (GFP) appeared in Goa, sparking rumors of a new front ahead of the 2027 assembly polls. AAP convenor Arvind Kejriwal announced he would make a significant declaration in the state. Conversely, Goa Congress president Girish Chodankar told reporters that alliance talks with the Vijai Sardesai-led GFP are still underway, confirming that the central leadership has not yet finalized a deal.
items.title: AAP and Congress vie for GFP alliance ahead of 2027 Goa polls

key_points: The sixth BRICS summit in Fortaleza produced the New Development Bank and Contingency Reserve Arrangement as key institutional outcomes.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi emphasized BRICS as a forward-looking institution while strengthening bilateral ties with China, Russia, Brazil, and South Africa.
India's new government used the platform to signal deeper engagement with South America and advocate for international governance reform.
items.summary: The sixth BRICS Summit held in Fortaleza on July 15 provided Prime Minister Narendra Modi a platform to present India's new global diplomatic vision. The summit resulted in three major documents, including the Agreement establishing the New Development Bank with $50 billion subscribed capital and the Treaty for the Contingency Reserve Arrangement. While some critics questioned BRICS' future, India's leadership highlighted its symbolic significance and geopolitical importance. During bilateral meetings, Modi engaged with leaders from China, Russia, Brazil, and South Africa to advance trade, defense, and strategic partnerships. Additionally, India signaled a renewed focus on South America through high-level outreach and proposed future forums.
items.title: Modi leads India at BRICS summit in Fortaleza to unveil new global vision

key_points: Mukherjee describes Varma as a feminist ahead of her time who chose to remain single and supported the freedom movement while raising many animals.
The article highlights Varma's autobiographical sketches in My Family and her short story Chini Feriwala, noting her witty and compassionate nature.
items.summary: Deputy Editor Anusua Mukherjee writes about seeing a peacock in Bengaluru, which reminds her of Hindi poet Mahadevi Varma's pet Neelkanth. Mukherjee notes that Varma, often called the modern Mira, was a feminist who chose to stay single and supported Gandhi's movement. She describes Varma as a witty and compassionate woman who raised many animals as friends. Mukherjee also discusses Varma's short story Chini Feriwala, which portrays a female narrator who maintains a friendship with a Chinese vendor despite societal pressure. The piece concludes by mentioning Varma's second home in Umagarh, which is now a museum.
items.title: Anusua Mukherjee profiles poet Mahadevi Varma and her pet peacock

key_points: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is expected to hold a bilateral meeting with Xi to discuss stabilizing bilateral ties and global issues.
items.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping has arrived in Delhi for the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit, marking his first visit to India since 2019. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is hosting the expanded grouping at Bharat Mandapam on September 12 and 13. The summit focuses on trade, investment, and global conflicts, with a bilateral meeting between Modi and Xi expected to address recent tensions. Chinese Ambassador Xu Feihong stated that Beijing is ready to strengthen communication and cooperation with New Delhi.
items.title: Chinese President Xi Jinping arrives in Delhi for BRICS Summit 2026

key_points: The Sensex declined 2.27% over five sessions ending September 11 while 17 BSE SmallCap stocks advanced each day.
ACE Equity identified 12 stocks that delivered cumulative returns between 10% and 30% during this period.
items.summary: Despite a 2.27% decline in the Sensex over five trading sessions ending September 11, approximately 17 BSE SmallCap stocks advanced each day. ACE Equity identified 12 of these stocks that gained for five consecutive days, delivering cumulative returns ranging from 10% to 30% during the period.
items.title: Twelve smallcap stocks gained for five consecutive trading sessions

key_points: Sugar Cosmetics valuation fell by nearly 80% as rising customer acquisition costs undermined its profitability despite a strong digital-first strategy.
Aluminium can shortages are forcing Indian beverage companies to use glass and PET bottles, while Arcil aims to recover bad loans from banks.
Copper prices crossed $14,500 per tonne due to supply uncertainty, and Aditya Birla Group entered the wires market with a ₹1,800 crore investment.
items.summary: This week's financial wrapup highlights several market shifts, starting with Sugar Cosmetics, whose valuation plummeted by nearly 80% from ₹2,700 crore. The company faces challenges as rising acquisition costs erode profits in a crowded D2C beauty sector. Meanwhile, aluminium shortages are pushing Indian beverage firms toward glass and PET packaging. In distressed assets, Arcil seeks to recover bad loans from banks, though valuations remain tricky. Copper prices surged past $14,500 per tonne on the LME amid supply concerns. Additionally, the Aditya Birla Group launched Ultravolt with ₹1,800 crore to challenge market leader Polycab in the growing wires and cables industry.
items.title: Sugar Cosmetics valuation drops 80% while copper prices surge
